utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The curtains are down. That is done in order to make the face distortion really effective. Therefore, though it looks as if we are in closed session, we are not. Due to technical problems this morning, we couldn't start any earlier. This raises an issue as to whether to continue with the present witness or with the next witness who has a keen interest in finishing his testimony today. I was informed that the parties would not disagree on interposing the next witness. Since I see no reaction I take it that the information is correct. That means that we first have to explain to Witness 65 that we'll move on and that he'll be on hold for a while, that we would then hear the parties on an application for protective measures for the next witness to be called and then we could continue with the next witness also a witness to be examined through a videolink. Could we, with all the protective measures in place, establish the videolink with Belgrade? Yes, good morning, Witness 65. Can you hear me? Can you see me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 65, we had quite a lot of technical problems this morning in The Hague which caused this late start. We even have a bigger problem, that is that the witness who would come after you has to leave today, which has caused us to decide that we would at this moment interrupt your testimony and that we would continue with you either later today or tomorrow. That certainly will be inconvenient to you. Unfortunately, we had no choice to decide otherwise. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I tried to explain to you that we have, due to these technical problems, that we have to interrupt your testimony at this moment and that another witness, who has -- who has to leave today, gets priority to give his testimony, and then we would continue with you after this witness has finished most likely today, that we would continue your examination after that. So then Ms. Gustafson would continue to put questions to you, and then Defence counsel would put questions to you as well. But do you now understand what I just told you, that you have to wait for a while?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So would you keep yourself available this morning so that if we would restart later this morning, that you would be available and if not, that we would tomorrow continue with your examination. So either later today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Whatever suits you. No problem for me. If you want, I can continue today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We don't know yet whether it will be later today or tomorrow. The representative of the Registry who is sitting next to you will inform you about the progress we are making. I would like to thank you very much for your flexibility at this moment, and the Chamber is grateful that you're willing to adapt to our problems. I again instruct you that you should meanwhile not speak with anyone about your testimony, the testimony you'd given yesterday or the testimony still to be given later today or tomorrow. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the representative of the Registry in Belgrade, I'd like to inform you that due to some technical matters, the change of interpreters teams, that we need to take a short break. We will take a break for, Mr. Registrar, is my assumption right that it would take a couple of minutes only? Yes. After these couple of minutes, we would like to start in private session with the next witness to be called in order to further hear answers to questions or submissions by the parties in relation to the protective measures requested in respect of this witness. We'll have a break, everyone is -- yes, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is with regard to the next witness. There is a question with regard to the issue of disclosure that might need to be dealt with just quite briefly before we proceed even with the issue concerning measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then after the break start with your submission on the -- what I understand to be late disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break for three to five minutes. --- Break taken at 10.43 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With all the protective measures in place, I would invite the witness to make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Witness 54. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 54, you are -- I'm not calling you by your own name because it was requested that protective measures are applied. Were you informed by the support officer of the victims and witness section what decision the Chamber has made? Were you informed -- were you informed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that no one can see your face, that no one can hear your own voice and that we will not use your own name, we'll call you by the number of Witness 54. Now, before you give evidence, the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Court wants to be assured that you will tell us whatever is asked in full accordance with the truth. That is you tell exactly how things were, that you do not add anything which is not what happened, that you do not leave out anything. And in order to be assured in these kinds of proceedings, the witness makes a solemn declaration. Do you understand what that means? That is that you are promising us that this is what you're going to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear? Then I do understand that the text of this solemn declaration has been given to you, and I'd invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Ms. Ley, you are going to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, questions will be put to you. You have met the witness before?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Questions will be put to you by Ms. Ley, and I do understand that you know her already because you've seen her before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting. With the previous witness, it's my recollection you asked whether there was anybody else present in the room. May I just take that one step further? As a result of something I just saw as the camera swept around, it appeared to me that there is some sort of glass partition there. I don't know whether there is anybody else who can actually see and be seen by the witness while this testimony is being taken. I would just like to have that clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness 54, I would like to know exactly who there are in the room where you're in, and I'd like to ask the representative of the Registry to tell us who are in the room and whether there is any visual connection of that room with any other room. Don't bother about it. Could the camera move or the -- yes. THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: Your Honours, present in the room are Witness 54, a technician and myself, and the only visual connection we have is with courtroom number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: Visual and audio connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing else. That would certainly satisfy Mr. Harvey. I take it, Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 54, now we come to what you came for, that is to answer the questions, questions first to be put to you by Ms. Ley. As I said you've met her before so it might be a familiar face for you on the screen. Please proceed, Ms. Ley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are at this moment in open session, Ms. Ley. If you want to get the details of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Ms. Ley, you certainly still will have in the back of your mind that identifying portions of the story should be dealt with in private session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: Witness 54, what was (redacted) doing for a living in 1998?

utterances.speaker: Witness 54
utterances.text: He worked as a car mechanic and car tire repairman.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: Witness 54
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: What about (redacted)? Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: Witness 54
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEY
utterances.text: I want you to please tell the Trial Chamber about the day that you saw (redacted) the last time. Can you tell us what happened, please?

utterances.speaker: Witness 54
utterances.text: Well, (redacted) from Novi Sad sent money, and (redacted) (redacted) went to the post office to collect the money. We were at my uncle's house, (redacted) is where we were living at the time. (redacted) came to fetch me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. We turn into private session. The witness is not able to -- and since you let him tell the story on his own, you are fully lacking control of what happens. We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness 54, very good of you to come and to answer the questions that have been put to you. (redacted) And I'd like to thank you, and I hope that you'll be home again very soon. This concludes your testimony. I think we should prepare for the next witness to appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: There is a matter before the next witness is called that I think I ought to raise, and I -- it might be an idea for us to do that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 65, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the witness. Now I can hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 65, can you also see us in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 65, we will now continue your examination, but I first of all would like to thank you for your flexibility to wait a while until we could resume, and I would also like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are starting from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we are not starting from the beginning. We will just continue. Ms. Gustafson will put further questions to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where we left off?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correctly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears I'm not getting translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you plugged into the right socket?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I didn't remove it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether you get the original. Witness 65, we are just checking whether Ms. Gustafson gets the right audio as well. So one --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm getting audio, Your Honour. It's just that I didn't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Can the counsel hear us now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. All technical problems resolved, Witness 65. We'll resume. And we'll continue where we stopped yesterday. Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 65. Yesterday evening, you had explained to the Trial Chamber what happened to your brother, and we appreciate your patience this morning. I would just like to ask you a few additional questions about some details of what happened to your brother, and I'd like, if you could, to listen to my questions as carefully as you can and to try to focus your answers just on the questions that I ask you, all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you said that the group that came and took your brother arrived in seven or eight vehicles. And I'd like to ask you, were you able to determine which -- were you able to determine which direction the vehicles came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came from the village, from Gllogjan, from that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So you're saying they came to the place where you were on the road coming in the -- from the direction of Gllogjan towards where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That goes to Dujak and Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'd like to ask you some questions about the people who came and took your brother. You said that one of them was wearing black clothes and had a black hood on his face. Was he the only one in black clothes or -- or were there more people wearing black clothes? Was it just one or was it more than one wearing black clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only him that was wearing black clothes. There were many other people present there. I couldn't count all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you also said that the person in black clothes had a black hide on his face. Was he the only one with a hood or were there others who were also wearing hoods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The other ones were not wearing black clothes, only he was wearing black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And do you remember anything about how any of the other ones were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing civilian clothes. The other ones, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And do you remember seeing any insignia or badges on any of the people's clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And were these people armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: What kind of arms did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were automatic rifles, these kinds of guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And what language did they speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And as far as you can -- you could tell, were these people members of some force or organisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, before the witness answers that question, an evidential foundation needs to be laid. Now, certain questions have been asked and certain answers have been given but to invite the witness at this stage to give an answer which amounts effectively to an expression of opinion, unless words were spoken or there is some other evidential foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, your rather abstract question, Mr. Emmerson, would like to you lay an evidentiary foundation for any conclusion to be drawn, and I think it would assist the Chamber if you would do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Witness 65, was anything said or done by these people to indicate to you that they belonged to some force or organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you last night as well about the case when they took my brother to the car and they beat me black and blue, and I lost my consciousness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like you, if you could, to listen carefully to my question. I asked you if these people said or did anything that indicated to you that they belonged to some force or some organisation? Do you remember anything that was said or done that indicated to you whether these people belonged to some group?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I intend to move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may do so. Sometimes the factual basis for observations can also be established once the observations have been made. I leave that up to you at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the people that day? Did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't. I couldn't recognise anyone. They took my brother to the car. I was lying on the ground. My wife poured some water on me because I was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you said one of them -- one of the men was looking for your cousin. Was anything said or done to indicate to you why they were looking for your cousin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't ask me the way you're putting it. They surrounded me and they were swearing and shouting, "Why are you here? You are siding with the Serbs. You are Maxhupis, gypsies." These were the words they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: When they said you were siding with the Serbs, what did you understand that to mean? Did you understand that to be a reference to something that you had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know what they were thinking. I don't know what was in their mind. I did not have any links with Serbs or Albanians, never. And I never had any problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you also said yesterday that the men pushed your wife and swore at her. Do you remember the words they used when they swore at your wife, what they said to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They said to her, "Maxhupis, Gipsy," because the way it happened was like this, they wanted to take me away and my wife screamed and was holding on to me, and other people were asking them not to take me away, and then they beat me. I remained down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And so -- so you were beaten and you were on the ground and you have also told us that they put your brother in a car, and they took him away. And I'd like to understand this from you. Did you actually see with your own eyes your brother being driven away, or did you not see them drive away with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see him being put into the car and being hit with a rifle's butt, and he was inside the car and then they drove him away. I could see them very well. I couldn't get up, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So you saw them drive away. Did they drive away the same way they had come or a different way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went in the same direction, from where they came.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, you've said that when the men arrived, they asked you where your cousin was and that you said you didn't know. And then eventually they took your brother --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Did they say -- did they say anything to you to indicate why they were taking your brother away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took him because of my cousin. My father told me that he had heard this being said. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You said your father told you that he had heard this being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had heard that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Did your father tell you he heard it that day? Or is this something your father heard later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, on the same day, while all these things were going on and the noise and everything. He was not close to me. He was sitting a little farther away. He was there. And now he's not alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I just want to clarify the last answer. Is this something your father heard said that day by the men who took your brother? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, yes, that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've said that you didn't recognise any of the men. Did you ever learn anything later about who any of these men were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't recognise anything. And I cannot tell you today who it was. I would like to know today who killed him and why. He was young. He was only 18 when he was taken away. He would be 24, 23 or 24 today.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And after that day when he was taken away, did you ever see your brother again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And what about other people in your family? Do you know if anyone in your family ever saw him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when he was taken away?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: After he was taken away, did anyone in your family ever see him again after he was taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there is just one more thing I'd like to ask you about on a different topic, and it's about the time before you left your home village, the village you grew up in, and I'd like to remind you not to mention the name of that village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: When you were living in your home village in 1998, before you left, had you heard of Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/65 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally hadn't heard. I didn't know what he was. I didn't know anything about the war. I don't know. We could hear some shots being fired in the mountains. That was all. But I didn't know who it was that was firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, before I give you an opportunity, Mr. Emmerson, to cross-examine the witness, I'd like to turn into private session for one second and seek one or two clarifications.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 65, these were the last questions put to you by Ms. Gustafson. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to the studio from where you gave your testimony. You've answered all the questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to drink some water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You can take off your earphones. This concludes your testimony. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the -- we do not need the videolink any more. Before I invite the Prosecution to call its next witness, I first would like to invite the parties to look what portions of today's evidence can be made public. I take it that you'll pass this message to Ms. Ley as well, Mr. Di Fazio. If the parties can agree on that, that would be preferable. The Chamber will then see. Before we continue I think there are some -- let me say it this way, there is no agreement yet on who to call next, that is the witness whose testimony was interrupted last week or whether it would be the witness Visnjic, but before we discuss this matter, that's at least the information I received, that -- I got an e-mail in which it is reported to the Chamber, and I'll just read one line. "I spoke with Mr. Re. He's insisting on putting Milan Visnjic before" and then the name of the witness whose testimony was interrupted last week. Now, we have made quite some progress. I do not know whether there is any issue remaining there but that depends on -- because the witness whose testimony was interrupted is, I think, invited to come back on Thursday. MR. DI FAZIO: That's the Prosecution's clear understanding and expectation. That's the arrangement that is in place as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then clear. How much time would we need for Mr. Visnjic if we would start with him now right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, I made some inquiries with the Prosecution yesterday, and my understanding is that Mr. Visnjic is travelling today and is therefore not available to testify until tomorrow. MR. DI FAZIO: That is correct. I can confirm, and I apologise. I should have alerted you sooner. We find ourselves in the position in the position of not being able to produce any witnesses for the last 15 minutes. What Mr. Emmerson just told you is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take it as a rule that if one party tells us something about very practical matters, that unless I hear from the other party, it's taken to be correct. So therefore, now, how much time would we need for the travelling witness, Mr. Visnjic? Tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think at the moment it's a matter for the Prosecution. Your Honour knows the position that we've taken in relation to that witness which is that the circumstances in which the material comes to be produced disentitled and disabled the defence from effective cross-examination, so depending upon what if any evidence the Prosecution intends to elicit from him in chief I would have expect the cross-examination to be short. But there has been a certain amount of recent disclosure which I will need to look at overnight, and I reserve my position. We certainly won't take the whole of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll be handling that witness, and although I haven't fully prepared my examination-in-chief, I don't expect it to be substantial by any means at all. I would have thought that probably about half an hour maximum would suffice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore there would be a fair expectation, I'm also looking at other Defence counsel, that tomorrow would do for the witness Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Most definitely tomorrow would do for the witness Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean for the next witness that we do not have to get in touch with VWS about travelling arrangements. We could just stick to Thursday, that witness to continue his testimony. MR. DI FAZIO: That's what the Prosecution completely envisages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's good to know. Are there any other procedural matters, since we have 30 minutes left?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There are in fact a number of exhibit issues that need to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is I have not prepared for this situation, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was going to suggest we perhaps deal with those at a convenient moment, tomorrow perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if there any time left tomorrow. We will prepare for that. Is there any other matter to be raised at this moment? MR. DI FAZIO: No, only that I'll raise this issue of procedural matters with my colleagues, as well, and that we'll notify the Defence and Trial Chamber of what those issues are, if in turn that could occur, I think it would help to expedite business if anything else arises. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, any matter you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just wanted to inquire through you, if I may, whether we have any report from Mr. Re or any of the representatives of the Prosecution about the late disclosure matter that was raised earlier and on which Mr. Re was going to get back to us? Perhaps that could wait until tomorrow. MR. DI FAZIO: No. No is the answer, if Your Honours please, but we'll attend to the matter and if the matter will be investigated, we'll be able to either provide an answer this afternoon by way of e-mail or address the matter tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for me, were you entirely exclusively addressing the matter of the statement being disclosed lately or also about other disclosure matters? Because it was not entirely clear to me whether there was any talking about facts, whether there was any other disclosure that needed attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It was that specific statement and its late disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Specifically. Then, I mean it has no -- it's an important matter, but not necessarily to be dealt with at this very moment. Of course, the Chamber would like to be kept abreast of the reasons why.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's the only reason I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to the parties how to inform the Chamber about that, although it should not be too informal. It should be somewhere on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn and -- until tomorrow, the 12th of September, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.35 p.m.,
